obs: "Kent v. Dulles, 357 U. S. 116 (1958), did invalidate a burden on the right to travel; however, the restriction was voided on the nonconstitutional basis that Congress did not intend to give the Secretary of State power to create the restriction at issue."
“Where the liberties of the citizen are involved, we said that we will construe narrowly all delegated powers that curtail or dilute them.”
"[The Court] stated that it would construe narrowly all delegated powers that curtail or dilute that right."
